questions.q: A mixture of ethanal and propanal is treated with dilute NaOH. How many β-hydroxy aldehydes (aldols) can form in total?
questions.explain: Both aldehydes have α-H, so there are two enolates and two acceptors: 2 × 2 = 4 aldols (two self and two crossed products).

questions.q: Benzaldehyde and acetophenone are warmed with dilute NaOH. The main product is:
questions.explain: In this Claisen–Schmidt condensation only acetophenone can form an enolate; it attacks benzaldehyde and the aldol dehydrates readily to the conjugated enone chalcone. Benzyl alcohol and benzoate would need concentrated alkali (Cannizzaro).

questions.q: Which pair of reactants in dilute NaOH would give the LEAST useful crossed aldol, i.e. a statistical mixture of products?
questions.explain: When both partners have α-H, each acts as donor and acceptor and four aldols form. In the other pairs one partner (HCHO or C₆H₅CHO) has no α-H and can serve only as the acceptor.

questions.q: Acetaldehyde is treated with excess formaldehyde in base. After all α-H atoms are replaced, a further crossed Cannizzaro reaction with more HCHO gives:
questions.explain: Three HCHO molecules replace the three α-H atoms to give (HOCH₂)₃C–CHO; the crossed Cannizzaro step then reduces its CHO to CH₂OH, giving pentaerythritol. (HOCH₂)₃C–CHO is the intermediate, not the final product.
